notes: מִי יִתֵּן takes its fixed optative rendering *Oh that* as one `noncompositional` unit; no morpheme's own lexeme is written in it, so the source head is the deterministic first token (rules 6, 30).

The italicized *that I had* in the second half is read as that one formula and the possessive recasting rewritten over the coordinated clause (rules 55, 25, 43); marking all three words `added` was the competing reading, and the italics corroborate without deciding (rule 7).

*which* is supplied for a finite clause juxtaposed to a written antecedent with no relative morpheme in the Hebrew, so it is `added` (rules 46, 55). אִישׁ רִיבִי → *adversary* fuses the generic head noun with its dependent under rule 30, headed on רִיב, while the suffix keeps its own *mine*.
Both marginal glosses ("Hebrew mark", "Hebrew book") were read and set aside (rule 38).
